title: Run proactive operations with Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric
author: kimani

content.text:
If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric.
AI is changing how every organization works. For most teams, the hard question isn't whether to use AI. It's how to turn it into real changes in daily operations: fewer surprises, faster responses, and better experiences for customers. Events often arrive faster than any person can respond. In the past, teams were limited by how quickly someone could read an alert and make a call. Now, agents can watch every signal and act in seconds, and each action and its outcome feed back into the system so it improves over time.
This isn't only about factory floors or connected devices. Every organization has events it wants to respond to:
• Catch an issue before it happens, such as a shipment running late or a system nearing capacity.
• Monitor processes and systems for anomalies, enabling a fix before something breaks.
• Automate entire workflows instead of handing work between teams.
• Improve the customer experience while the customer is still engaged.
TransGrid Energy uses Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Intelligence to turn live data-center telemetry into better operational outcomes. By bringing power, cooling, battery, and equipment data together with real-time alarm rules and its WattSchema ontology, TransGrid can identify potential failures before they happen and optimize cooling or battery use as operating conditions and energy prices change. Data-center operators can improve uptime, efficiency, and cost control without building and maintaining complex data-movement infrastructure.
“We want to focus on our business problems, not our data movement problems. Fabric Real-Time Intelligence handles this for us so we can focus on our business”
Tony Guidici - CTO / Head of Digital Service, TransGrid Energy, LLC
At Ignite, we're announcing new capabilities in Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric that make it simpler to stream, analyze, and act on event data. We're helping our customers move from waiting for something to fail and reacting, to predicting that it might fail and getting ahead of it.
Figure: Real-Time Intelligence connects streaming, analysis, and action in a continuous loop.
Stream: Connect to real-time data wherever it lives
Every organization already has streaming data, from applications, databases, devices, and logs. For years, putting it to work was a project of its own. The data lived across clouds and systems, and every source needed its own pipeline. Ingesting, storing, querying, and alerting each took a separate tool, with its own security model, its own bill, and its own specialists. The cost and complexity stalled many projects before they delivered anything.
Real-Time Intelligence changes that. Working with streaming data no longer takes a specialist. With Eventstream, you can connect Kafka, Amazon Kinesis, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, MQTT, and database change data capture, then filter, transform, and route events without writing code. If it produces events, Fabric can take them. Real-Time hub, built into every Fabric tenant, gives you one place to discover and manage all of it, with nothing to set up. And because it's part of Fabric, streaming data gets the same security, governance, and cost management as the rest of your data.
What's new for streaming
Event Hubs shortcuts (Preview)
Many teams already run their event pipelines on Azure Event Hubs. We're introducing Event Hubs shortcuts so you can bring an event hub you already run into Fabric as an eventstream, without an extra copy. You keep control in Azure, and you can filter, transform, and route events to Eventhouse, lakehouse, Activator, and more.
Native Eventstream routing endpoint in Azure IoT Hub (Generally Available)
Many device solutions already send their telemetry through Azure IoT Hub. Eventstream is now a native routing endpoint in IoT Hub, so you can send device data straight into Fabric using the routing rules, filters, and message enrichments you already have. You get from device telemetry to real-time insights, alerts, and automated actions faster, and you can combine telemetry with device-state events for a fuller view of your operations.
Figure: Fabric Eventstream is now a native endpoint in Azure IoT Hub for message routing.
Business events as a source and destination in Eventstream (Generally Available)
Some of the most useful signals are business moments, like a shipment running late. Business events let you define them once and share them across Fabric. We're making them generally available as both a source and a destination in Eventstream, so you can route business events like any other stream, or turn live data into new ones that Activator, notebooks, and other Fabric items act on.
Together, these updates let you use the streams you already have and turn them into signals the rest of Fabric can act on.
Figure: Bringing an existing Azure event hub into Fabric as an eventstream.
Analyze: Make sense of fast-changing data
Analyzing real-time data is different from analyzing a nightly report. Events arrive in high volume, often as semi-structured JSON or logs, and the questions change as conditions change. Tools built for batch reporting weren't designed for that. By the time the data was loaded and modeled, the moment had passed, and stale data isn't insight. It's history.
Operational data is complex. Understanding it shouldn't be. Eventhouse is purpose-built for event, log, and time-series data, with sub-second queries at petabyte scale, so you can ask new questions of fresh data in KQL or SQL, or in plain language with Copilot. Real-Time Dashboards show what's happening as it happens, and Fabric Maps show where. And because it all sits on OneLake, your real-time data isn't siloed from the rest of your data estate.
Figure: A Real-Time Dashboard and map showing what's happening, and where, as it happens.
What's new for analysis
Outbound access protection and Customer-Managed Keys for Eventhouse (Generally Available)
Real-time workloads need the same protections as the rest of your data. We're extending two of them to every Eventhouse scenario. Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) give you direct control over the encryption keys that protect your data and metadata in Eventhouse. Outbound access protection blocks Eventhouse from sending data anywhere you haven't explicitly allowed, now including connections to Event Hubs and Eventstream, which helps prevent data exfiltration.
Smart caching and update policies for OneLake shortcuts in Eventhouse (Preview)
Eventhouse can query data where it already lives in OneLake through shortcuts, and query acceleration keeps those queries fast. We're making that smarter and simpler. Eventhouse now tunes the acceleration cache automatically based on real query patterns, instead of a fixed, manually set window, so frequently queried data stays fast and you get better price-performance with no tuning. And you can now attach update policies to accelerated shortcuts, so transformations run continuously as new data lands in the lake, with no separate pipeline.
Together, these updates let you analyze real-time data with the same protections as the rest of your estate and get fast answers from the data you already have in OneLake.
Proactive Eventhouse monitoring (Preview)
To optimize your real-time setup, you need a clear, at-a-glance view of what's happening, so you can react appropriately. Three new Workspace Monitoring logs give you that visibility:
• Capacity Throttling Events – Identify when an Eventhouse enters throttling and understand the different throttling stages.
• Sub-Optimal Eventhouse Size – Detect when an Eventhouse remains undersized due to capacity constraints, signaling a need for capacity or workload optimization.
• Scale-Out Events – Understand why an Eventhouse scaled out, including resource utilization, ingestion load, and query acceleration.
A ready-to-use Real-Time Dashboard template brings these logs together, and Activator can alert you as soon as something changes. You can fix capacity and performance issues before they affect your workloads, and size your capacity with confidence.
AI-native custom visual builder in Real-Time Dashboard (Preview)
Standard dashboard charts don't always fit the way an operations team works, and building something custom has meant writing visualization code.
AI Custom visual brings a new way to create custom dashboard experiences in Real-Time Dashboard by allowing users to describe the visual they need in natural language and generate it instantly, without writing visualization code.
Figure: Create custom dashboard visuals using natural language with Copilot.
Teams can go beyond standard charts and build visuals tailored to how they actually operate, from a service-health command center to workflow-specific monitoring, without waiting on a developer.
Because it generates both the query and the visual, anyone on the team can build the view they need and share complex insights more clearly.
Act: Turn signals into action
If data flows into dashboards but nobody acts on it, it doesn't change outcomes. For most teams, acting on real-time data has meant someone watching. Issues were discovered late, there were more assets than anyone could watch, alerts arrived without the context to act on them, and every response depended on a manual handoff.
Activator acts the moment conditions change: a known condition triggers a configured response, like notifying a shipment's owner the instant it gets too warm and starting the workflow. Operations Agents help you get ahead of what's coming: they monitor your goals, investigate what's changing, and recommend the next step for your approval, so your team stays in control.
What's new for action
Operations Agent observability (Generally Available)
Handing an agent more responsibility takes trust, and trust takes visibility. Operations Agent observability shows what your agent observed, decided, and did, in its Activity screens or in your Workspace Monitoring eventhouse. Your team can audit every recommendation and action and troubleshoot faster, so you can expand what the agent handles with confidence.
Ontology context for Operations Agents (Preview)
An agent is only as good as the context underneath it. Operations Agents can now use your Fabric IQ ontology as context, reasoning about the entities and relationships that make up your business instead of raw tables. Their monitoring and recommendations reflect how your operations actually work, so they're more relevant and easier to act on.
Activator as a publisher of business events (Generally Available)
The business events you can stream and analyze can now start in Activator too. When an Activator rule fires, it can publish a business event that other Fabric items, agents, and flows subscribe to, so one detected condition can set off a coordinated response across your organization, without custom integration.
Together, these updates help you act on more of what's happening, with the context and visibility to trust what your agents do.
Figure: Animated GIF - An Operations Agent recommends a next step in Teams, and the team approves it.
Get started
Real-Time Intelligence is generally available in Microsoft Fabric today. To get started, use the following resources:
• Follow the end-to-end Real-Time Intelligence tutorial to stream, analyze, and act on sample data.
• Join a Real-Time Intelligence in a Day workshop to build a solution hands-on.
• Work with a Real-Time Intelligence featured partner to plan your first deployment.
